en.r: The largest national park in Alberta's Rocky Mountains, north of Banff and west of Edmonton. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984, with the glaciers of the Columbia Icefield, lakes, waterfalls and hot springs.
en.h: It began as Jasper Forest Park on 14 September 1907 and became a national park in 1930. The Grand Trunk Pacific railway arrived in 1911 and founded the town now called Jasper. In 1908 explorer Mary Schäffer reached Maligne Lake using a map drawn by Nakoda guide Samson Beaver.
en.ff: At least 50 mammal species, including moose, elk, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, grizzly bears and wolves.

en.r: In Alberta's southwest corner, where the Rockies meet the prairie, on the border with Montana's Glacier National Park. Together they form the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
en.h: Canada's fourth national park, it began in 1895 as the Kootenay Lakes Forest Reserve, at the suggestion of rancher Frederick Godsal. In 1932 it joined the neighbouring US park to form the world's first international peace park.
en.ff: More than 1,000 plant species, about 20 found nowhere else. Grizzly and black bears, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, elk, cougars and bison.

en.r: A national park that existed from 1909 to 1940 near Wainwright, in east-central Alberta, created to save the plains bison from extinction. The land is now Canadian Forces Base Wainwright.
en.h: It was one of the prairie "regeneration parks" meant to restore bison and pronghorn. It closed in 1940, was delisted in 1947 and the land went to the Department of National Defence. Its first warden was Bud Cotton, from 1912 to 1940.
en.ff: Its focus was the plains bison, often called "buffalo". The recovery worked so well that the park became overcrowded.
at: Now a military area, not open as a park

pt.r: A 35 km de Edmonton, em Alberta, é o maior parque nacional do Canadá totalmente cercado. Teve papel decisivo na salvação do bisão-das-planícies.
pt.h: A região de Beaver Hills abrigou por séculos manadas de uapitis, bisões e alces, e há mais de 200 sítios de acampamentos indígenas. O parque nasceu como reserva de uapitis e virou parque nacional em 1913; bisões criados ali repovoaram outras áreas do Canadá e dos EUA.

en.r: 35 km from Edmonton, Alberta, it is Canada's largest fully fenced national park. It played a key role in saving the plains bison.
en.h: The Beaver Hills sheltered herds of elk, bison and moose for centuries, and there are over 200 Indigenous campsite remains. The park began as an elk reserve and became a national park in 1913; bison raised here restocked other areas of Canada and the US.
en.ff: It has Canada's highest density of hoofed mammals: plains and wood bison, elk, moose and deer. It also hosts North America's largest and smallest land mammals, the wood bison and the pygmy shrew. More than 250 bird species.

es.r: A 35 km de Edmonton, en Alberta, es el mayor parque nacional totalmente cercado de Canadá. Tuvo un papel clave en la salvación del bisonte de las llanuras.

es.ff: Tiene la mayor densidad de grandes herbívoros de Canadá: bisontes de llanura y de bosque, uapitíes, alces y ciervos. Alberga además el mayor y el menor mamífero terrestre de América del Norte, el bisonte de bosque y la musaraña pigmea. Más de 250 especies de aves.

en.r: A former national park north of the former community of Nemiskam, now a ghost town, in south-central Alberta, created in 1922 to protect pronghorn, which were nearly extinct. It closed in 1947 and was delisted in 1947.
en.h: It was one of the prairie "regeneration parks", like Buffalo, Nemiskam, Wawaskesy and Menissawok, meant to restore bison and pronghorn. Once the herds recovered, the parks were closed. Nemiskam is a Blackfoot word meaning "between two valleys".
en.ff: Its focus was the pronghorn, North America's fastest land mammal.
at: No visitor facilities today

en.r: A former national park north of Medicine Hat, in southeastern Alberta, created in 1922 to protect pronghorn, which were nearly extinct. It closed in 1938 and was delisted in 1947.
en.h: It was one of the prairie "regeneration parks", like Buffalo, Nemiskam, Wawaskesy and Menissawok, meant to restore bison and pronghorn. Once the herds recovered, the parks were closed. Wawaskesy is the Cree word for pronghorn. In 1941 the land became part of the Suffield military block.
en.ff: Its focus was the pronghorn, North America's fastest land mammal.
at: Now a military area (Suffield)

t.pt: O Winagami Wildland Provincial Park é um parque provincial selvagem no Canadá. Tem 65,4 km² e está protegido desde 1956, sob gestão do governo provincial. Na classificação da IUCN, está na categoria II, a dos parques nacionais: protege ecossistemas inteiros e recebe visitantes.
t.en: Winagami Wildland Provincial Park is a wildland provincial park in Canada. It covers 65.4 km² and has been protected since 1956. It is managed by the provincial government. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
